age75Increase.rule: Automatic 10% increase the month after the 75th birthday.

residence.rule: At least 10 years of residence in Canada since age 18 to qualify while living in Canada. Fewer than 40 years gives a partial pension of (years in Canada / 40) of the full amount.

sources.covers: 10 years since 18 (living in Canada); 20 years since 18 (living outside Canada)
partial pension = years lived in Canada / 40

deferral.rule: Deferring after 65: +0.6% per month (7.2% a year), up to 36% at age 70.

recoveryTax.rule: Repay 15% of net world income above the minimum threshold, until the whole pension is recovered.
recoveryTax.note: The ESDC quarterly tables list the $95,323 threshold with an upper bound that moves each quarter with the pension (Q1 $154,708/$160,647; Q2 $154,753/$160,696; Q3 $155,109/$161,088; Q4 $155,320/$161,320). The upper bound follows from the threshold plus the annual pension divided by 0.15, not a separately legislated figure.

paidAbroad.rule: OAS can be received while living outside Canada only with at least 20 years of residence in Canada after 18.
paidAbroad.caveat: The 20-year rule was read on the page. The commonly stated consequence for fewer than 20 years (paid for 6 months of absence, then suspended) was not read on a fetched page; see uncertain.

gis.incomeCutoffNote: Annual income cutoff for a single person; OAS and GIS themselves are not counted as income.

baseRate.rule: GIS is reduced by $1 for every $2 of income other than OAS and GIS (50 cents on the dollar).

sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada (Question Period Note)
Employment and Social Development Canada (Evaluation Directorate)

earningsExemption.rule: The first $5,000 of employment and self-employment income is fully exempt; on earnings from $5,000 to $15,000, 50% is exempt, so only half counts. In force since July 2020.
earningsExemption.correctionToBrief: The band on the next $10,000 is a 50% exemption, not 25%. The 25% figure belongs to the GIS top-up's reduction rate (below).

topUp.rule: The GIS top-up (added 2011) is reduced by $0.25 per dollar of other income above a threshold ($2,048 single, $4,096 couple, as of the 2017 report), so the combined reduction in that band is 75 cents on the dollar.
topUp.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada (Evaluation Directorate)
topUp.caveat: The thresholds are from 2017. No official page read gave the 2026 top-up threshold or amount.

livingInCanadaOnly.rule: You must live in Canada. GIS stops after more than 6 months outside Canada, regardless of years of residence.

sources.covers: out of the country more than 6 months become ineligible

contributions2026.note: The 5.95% employee rate is the base 4.95% plus the first additional 1.0% (self-employed 9.9% + 2.0% = 11.9%).

firstAdditional.caveat: The page confirms 1.0% for a total of 5.95%. The 2% self-employed figure follows from the self-employed paying both shares (11.9% total on the CRA page) and was not read as its own line.

secondAdditionalCPP2.caveat: The page states the 4% employee and employer rate and the $832 self-employed maximum; 8% is derived from those (2 x 4% x $10,400 = $832).

baseReplacement.rule: Base CPP replaces one quarter (25%) of average adjusted pensionable earnings; the enhancement grows this to one third (33.33%) for earnings after 2019.

generalDropout.rule: Up to 17% of the contributory period with the lowest earnings, a maximum of 8 years, is excluded from the base component calculation.
generalDropout.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada (CPP Annual Report, fiscal year ending March 31, 2024)

early.rule: -0.6% per month before 65 (7.2% a year), maximum -36% at 60.

late.rule: +0.7% per month after 65 (8.4% a year), maximum +42% at 70.

paidAbroad.rule: CPP benefits are paid no matter where the recipient lives in the world.

nonResidentTax.rule: Non-resident tax withheld at 25% standard, reducible by tax treaty.

ontarioGAINS.rule: Paid to low-income Ontario seniors who receive OAS and GIS; reduced as private income rises; a single senior with annual private income up to $4,416 remains eligible. Residence: Canada 10 years and Ontario for the past 12 months or 20 years in total since 18.

bcSeniorsSupplement.rule: $1.00 to $99.30 a month for a single senior who receives OAS and GIS and is a permanent resident of B.C.

meta.method: Each figure was fetched from the cited page on 2026-09-30. 'date' is the page's own 'Date modified' or the report date. confirmed=true means the figure was read on that page, not taken from a search summary.

uncertain: OAS abroad with fewer than 20 years of residence: the 6-months-then-suspended rule was not read on a fetched page (the OAS 'living outside Canada' URL returned 404). Only the 20-year requirement for living outside Canada is confirmed.
The GIS top-up's 2026 threshold and amount were not found. The $0.25-per-dollar rate and the $2,048 single threshold come from a 2017 ESDC report.
The brief's '25% band on the next $10,000' does not match the sources: earnings from $5,000 to $15,000 are 50% exempt. The 25% rate is the top-up's reduction rate.

The self-employed rates for the first additional contribution (2%) and CPP2 (8%) are derived from the self-employed paying both shares and from the CRA maximums ($8,460.90, $832), not read as stand-alone lines.
CPP's 25% non-resident withholding came from a search summary of canada.ca pages, not a direct page read (confirmed=false).
The OAS full-recovery upper bound differs by quarter in the ESDC tables; the recovery-tax page gives $155,320 / $161,320 for July 2027 - June 2028 (2026 income).
Base contribution rate split (4.95% base + 1.0% first additional) is standard but was not read as a separate line on the CRA page; the page gives 5.95% total.
